name: Carousel
description: Carousel is a Manipulation Rummy game where players can rearrange existing melds on the table to create new combinations. Players draw 1-3 cards per turn and must meld after drawing 1 or 2 cards. Features jokers and a knocking mechanic to end rounds.

overview.description: Carousel is a Manipulation Rummy game where players can rearrange existing melds on the table to create new combinations. Players draw 1-3 cards per turn and must meld after drawing 1 or 2 cards. Features jokers and a knocking mechanic to end rounds.

history.origins: Carousel appears in Culbertson's Hoyle (1950) and was described by John Scarne in his Encyclopedia of Card Games (1973) as 'fairly popular and interesting.' It is part of the Manipulation Rummy family where table melds can be rearranged.
timeline: 1973: Described by John Scarne in Encyclopedia of Card Games
Current: Part of the Manipulation Rummy family including Machiavelli, Vatikan, Shanghai
history.cultural: Popular among rummy enthusiasts who enjoy the strategic depth of manipulating table melds. The game rewards careful planning and spatial reasoning.
history.evolution: Two main versions exist: Scarne's version (draw 1-3 cards, knock with â‰¤5 points) and Culbertson's earlier version (draw up to 4, knock with â‰¤10 points at start of turn only).

setup.players: 2-5 players, each playing individually. 2 players: use 53 cards (1 deck + 1 joker). 3-5 players: use 106 cards (2 decks + 2 jokers).
setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack(s) with jokers. 2 players: 1 deck + 1 joker = 53 cards. 3-5 players: 2 decks + 2 jokers = 106 cards. Cards rank A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2. Ace high or low in sequences (not both).
setup.dealing: 10 cards dealt to each player. Remaining cards form stock. No discard pile in this game.
setup.equipment: 1-2 standard decks with jokers, score sheet

rules.objective: Get rid of cards by melding. Knock when hand totals â‰¤5 points to end round. Lowest hand wins round. First to 150+ points ends game and scores bonuses.
rules.gameplay: Turn: Must draw 1st card, then either meld OR draw 2nd card. If drew 2nd, must either meld OR draw 3rd card. If drew 3rd card, cannot meld this turn. No discard pile - only draw and meld. Melds: sequences (3+ same suit, Ace high or low not both) or groups (3+ same rank, different suits). Jokers wild. Key feature: Can rearrange ALL table melds when melding, breaking up existing sets and reforming them, provided you add at least one new card from hand and all table cards end in valid melds. Joker value fixed when played, can be moved if released by substituting actual card it represents. Released joker must be used immediately in new meld, cannot return to hand. Knock: After melding with â‰¤5 points in hand, can knock to end round. No layoffs. Winner has lowest hand. Scoring: Winner scores differences from other players' hands. If winner is not knocker, gets 10-point undercut bonus. Going out completely: 25 bonus. Game to 150: winner gets 100 bonus, all get 25 per hand won.
keyRules: Draw 1-3 cards per turn; must meld after 1 or 2 draws
Can rearrange ALL table melds when playing
Must add at least one new card from hand when melding
Sequences: 3+ same suit, Ace high or low (not both)
Jokers wild, value fixed when played
Released joker must be used immediately
Knock with â‰¤5 points to end round
Undercut bonus if winner didn't knock

strategy.basic: Focus on reducing hand value. Meld early to get cards out, but remember that table melds help opponents manipulate. Knock when you have a low hand.
strategy.intermediate: Track which cards have been played to estimate what opponents hold. Plan manipulation moves in advance - visualize how you can rearrange table melds before your turn. Use jokers strategically.
strategy.advanced: Control the pace by deciding when to meld. Sometimes holding cards is better than helping opponents with table melds. Complex manipulation chains can empty your hand in one turn. Knock timing is crucial - too early and someone might undercut; too late and opponent may go out completely.
tips: Hoarding cards is common - everyone waits for others to meld first
Jokers are powerful but worth 25 points if stuck in hand
Look for manipulation opportunities that use multiple cards from your hand
Knocking with exactly 5 is risky - others may have less
Going out completely for 25 bonus is often worth the risk
Track high cards - they're worth the most stuck in hands

scoring.description: Points for cards left in hand when someone knocks; lowest total wins.
scoring.winCondition: Lowest total points when a player knocks and round ends; reach target or fewest points wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: Manipulation Rummy: draw 1-3 cards, meld or rearrange table melds; jokers wild; knock to end round.
